11.overview: The empty city of 7:4 is filled. The leaders live in Jerusalem, one family in ten is chosen by lot to move there, and the people bless those who volunteer (vv. 1-2). The residents are listed: 468 valiant men of the line of Perez and 928 of Benjamin (vv. 3-9); 1,192 priests under Seraiah, ruler of the house of God (vv. 10-14); 284 Levites, with Mattaniah of the sons of Asaph the leader of the praise (vv. 15-18); 172 gatekeepers (v. 19); the temple servants on Ophel, the singers under a royal provision, and Pethahiah of the sons of Zerah at the king's side (vv. 20-24). Then the villages of Judah, from Hebron and Beersheba to Lachish and Azekah — so they encamped from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom — and of Benjamin, from Geba to Lod and Ono (vv. 25-36).

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Now the leaders of the people lived in Jerusalem. And the rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of ten to live in Jerusalem the holy city, while nine out of ten remained in the other towns (v. 1). And the people blessed all the men who willingly offered to live in Jerusalem (v. 2).
verseByVerse.theology: The empty city of 7:4 is filled by a tithe of the people: one family in ten, chosen by lot, and others who volunteered. They gave God a tenth of their harvest in chapter 10; here they give him a tenth of themselves.

verseByVerse.quote: Now the leaders of the people lived in Jerusalem. And the rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of ten to live in Jerusalem the holy city, while nine out of ten remained in the other towns. And the people blessed all the men who willingly offered to live in Jerusalem.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Now the leaders of the people lived in Jerusalem. And the rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of ten to live in Jerusalem the holy city, while nine out of ten remained in the other towns.

The problem was stated in 7:4: the city was wide and large, but the people within it were few. A wall round an empty city defends nothing. So the leaders move in, and the rest cast lots, and one family in every ten packs up and moves to Jerusalem. It was a tithe of the people. The chapter before, they had promised God a tenth of their crops (10:37-38); now they give him a tenth of themselves.

It was not an easy lot to draw. Jerusalem was the most exposed place in the province, hated by its neighbours, short of houses, and far from the fields that fed a family. The towns were safer and the farms were there. To move meant leaving land your family worked for a half-built city on a hill.

Jerusalem the holy city. Isaiah had called her that — put on your beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city (Isa 52:1) — and the name followed her into the Gospels, where the devil took him to the holy city and set him on the pinnacle of the temple (Matt 4:5). But its last use is the one this chapter is reaching for: I saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God ... Behold, the dwelling place of God is with man (Rev 21:2-3). There, nobody has to be chosen by lot to live in it.

And the people blessed all the men who willingly offered to live in Jerusalem. Some did not wait for the lot. They volunteered, and the people blessed them for it. The verb is the one the psalm uses of the Messiah's people: Your people will offer themselves freely on the day of your power (Ps 110:3). That is still the mark of Christ's people: not conscripts but volunteers. A question to bring before God: in the place he has put you, is there a harder post that needs someone to offer, and have you been waiting to be chosen for it?

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 3–24 — The Chiefs Who Lived in Jerusalem
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The heads of the province who lived in Jerusalem: sons of Judah, 468 of the line of Perez (vv. 3-6), and of Benjamin, 928 (vv. 7-9); priests, 1,192 in three groups, with Seraiah ruler of the house of God (vv. 10-14); Levites, 284, among them Mattaniah of the sons of Asaph, the leader of the praise (vv. 15-18); gatekeepers, 172 (v. 19). The rest lived in their towns; the temple servants on Ophel; the singers under a royal provision; and Pethahiah, of the sons of Zerah, served at the king's side (vv. 20-24).
verseByVerse.theology: A city of soldiers, priests, singers and gatekeepers: valiant men and the leader of the praise on the same list. The holy city needed both.

verseByVerse.quote: These are the chiefs of the province who lived in Jerusalem; but in the towns of Judah everyone lived on his property in their towns: Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple servants, and the descendants of Solomon's servants. And in Jerusalem lived certain of the sons of Judah and of the sons of Benjamin. Of the sons of Judah: Athaiah the son of Uzziah, son of Zechariah, son of Amariah, son of Shephatiah, son of Mahalalel, of the sons of Perez; and Maaseiah the son of Baruch, son of Col-hozeh, son of Hazaiah, son of Adaiah, son of Joiarib, son of Zechariah, son of the Shilonite. All the sons of Perez who lived in Jerusalem were 468 valiant men. And these are the sons of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, son of Joed, son of Pedaiah, son of Kolaiah, son of Maaseiah, son of Ithiel, son of Jeshaiah, and his brothers, men of valor, 928. Joel the son of Zichri was their overseer; and Judah the son of Hassenuah was second over the city.
verseByVerse.commentary:
These are the chiefs of the province who lived in Jerusalem. Then the names, family by family, with their ancestry traced back several generations. First Judah: of the sons of Perez, and all the sons of Perez who lived in Jerusalem were 468 valiant men (v. 6).

Perez was one of the twin sons of Judah by Tamar, and from Perez came Boaz, David, and the kings (Ruth 4:18-22). The family of the royal line moved into the city of David. And in verse 24 the other twin appears: Pethahiah, of the sons of Zerah the son of Judah. Matthew names them both at the start of the genealogy of Jesus: Judah the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar (Matt 1:3). Both branches of that unlikely family were living in Jerusalem when Nehemiah wrote.

Then Benjamin, men of valor, 928, under Joel son of Zichri, with Judah son of Hassenuah second over the city. Together 1,396 fighting men from the two tribes. The holy city still needed soldiers.

verseByVerse.quote: Of the priests: Jedaiah the son of Joiarib, Jachin, Seraiah the son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, ruler of the house of God, and their brothers who did the work of the house, 822; and Adaiah the son of Jeroham, son of Pelaliah, son of Amzi, son of Zechariah, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah, and his brothers, heads of fathers' houses, 242; and Amashsai, the son of Azarel, son of Ahzai, son of Meshillemoth, son of Immer, and their brothers, mighty men of valor, 128; their overseer was Zabdiel the son of Haggedolim.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The priests, in three groups: those who did the work of the house, 822; heads of fathers' houses, 242; and mighty men of valor, 128. Together 1,192. At their head is Seraiah the son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok ... ruler of the house of God (v. 11). The name runs back through Hilkiah, the high priest who found the book of the law in Josiah's day, to Zadok, Solomon's high priest. The line of the high priests had come through the exile unbroken.

And notice that some of the priests are called mighty men of valor. The men who served at the altar were also men of courage. In a city under threat, holiness and bravery were not two different kinds of people.

verseByVerse.quote: And of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, son of Bunni; and Shabbethai and Jozabad, of the chiefs of the Levites, who were over the outside work of the house of God; and Mattaniah the son of Mica, son of Zabdi, son of Asaph, who was the leader of the praise, who gave thanks, and Bakbukiah, the second among his brothers; and Abda the son of Shammua, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun. All the Levites in the holy city were 284. The gatekeepers, Akkub, Talmon and their brothers, who kept watch at the gates, were 172.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The Levites: Shemaiah, and Shabbethai and Jozabad, who were over the outside work of the house of God, the repairs and supplies that kept the temple running. Then Mattaniah the son of Mica, son of Zabdi, son of Asaph, who was the leader of the praise, who gave thanks. Asaph was David's chief musician, and twelve of the psalms bear his name (Pss 50, 73-83). Five centuries on, his descendant is leading the thanksgiving in the rebuilt temple.

All the Levites in the holy city were 284. Then the gatekeepers, Akkub, Talmon and their brothers, who kept watch at the gates, were 172. The gates Nehemiah had hung (7:1) now had men to keep them. Praise inside and watchmen at the doors: that is still what a church needs.

verseByVerse.quote: And the rest of Israel, and of the priests and the Levites, were in all the towns of Judah, every one in his inheritance. But the temple servants lived on Ophel; and Ziha and Gishpa were over the temple servants. The overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi the son of Bani, son of Hashabiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Mica, of the sons of Asaph, the singers, over the work of the house of God. For there was a command from the king concerning them, and a fixed provision for the singers, as every day required. And Pethahiah the son of Meshezabel, of the sons of Zerah the son of Judah, was at the king's side in all matters concerning the people.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And the rest of Israel, and of the priests and the Levites, were in all the towns of Judah, every one in his inheritance. His inheritance: the family land allotted in Joshua's day, returned to after the exile. The nine in ten who stayed were not failing to answer a call. They were living on the land God had promised them.

The temple servants lived on Ophel, the ridge where they had built their stretch of wall (3:26). The overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi ... of the sons of Asaph, the singers. And there was a command from the king concerning them, and a fixed provision for the singers, as every day required. The king is probably the Persian king, who had already exempted the singers from tax (Ezra 7:24). If so, an emperor who worshipped other gods was paying the daily wages of the choir that sang the psalms of Asaph to the LORD.

And Pethahiah the son of Meshezabel, of the sons of Zerah the son of Judah, was at the king's side in all matters concerning the people. A Jew at the Persian king's side on behalf of his people, a post not unlike Nehemiah's own at Susa. God always had someone at that door.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 25–36 — From Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The people of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba, Dibon, Beersheba, Ziklag, Zorah, Adullam, Lachish, Azekah and their villages — so they encamped from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom (vv. 25-30). The people of Benjamin lived from Geba through Michmash, Bethel, Anathoth, Nob and Ramah to Lod and Ono (vv. 31-35), and some Levites of Judah were assigned to Benjamin (v. 36).
verseByVerse.theology: Every name on the list is a town God had given their fathers, and nearly every one has a story. The nine in ten were not second-class; they were living on the promise too.

verseByVerse.quote: And as for the villages, with their fields, some of the people of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba and its villages, and in Dibon and its villages, and in Jekabzeel and its villages, and in Jeshua and in Moladah and Beth-pelet, in Hazar-shual, in Beersheba and its villages, in Ziklag, in Meconah and its villages, in En-rimmon, in Zorah, in Jarmuth, Zanoah, Adullam, and their villages, Lachish and its fields, and Azekah and its villages. So they encamped from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And as for the villages, with their fields, some of the people of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba and its villages. Kiriath-arba is the old name of Hebron (Josh 14:15), where Abraham bought a grave and David was first crowned. Then Beersheba, where Abraham dug his wells; Ziklag, which the Philistine king gave to David; Zorah, where Samson was born; Adullam, where David hid in the cave; Lachish and Azekah, the last fortresses to hold out against Babylon. Every town on the list is a chapter of their history, and every one was lived in again.

So they encamped from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom. The old measure of the land was from Dan to Beersheba, the whole country north to south. Now it runs from Beersheba to the edge of Jerusalem: a strip of hill country, a fraction of what they had once held. And they encamped, the word used of Israel in the wilderness. They were back in the land, and still living like pilgrims in it.

The Valley of Hinnom, the northern limit of Judah's settlement, is the valley of Topheth, where Judah's kings had once burned their children in the fire, which I did not command, nor did it come into my mind (Jer 7:31). Its name in the Greek of the Gospels is Gehenna, the word Jesus used for hell. The people lived right up to the edge of the place of their worst sin, in a land that had been given back to them. They were pilgrims looking for more than that strip of hill country could give. So are we: here we have no lasting city, but we seek the city that is to come (Heb 13:14).

verseByVerse.quote: The people of Benjamin also lived from Geba onward, at Michmash, Aija, Bethel and its villages, Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah, Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim, Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat, Lod, and Ono, the valley of craftsmen. And certain divisions of the Levites in Judah were assigned to Benjamin.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The people of Benjamin also lived from Geba onward, at Michmash, Aija, Bethel and its villages, Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah, Hazor, Ramah. Michmash, where Jonathan climbed the cliff; Bethel, where Jacob saw the ladder; Anathoth, Jeremiah's town; Ramah, Samuel's home. And Nob, the city of the priests, which Saul put to the sword, man and woman, child and infant (1 Sam 22:19). The town of a massacre is a town of families again.

On to Lod, and Ono, the valley of craftsmen — the plain where Sanballat had tried to lure Nehemiah (6:2), home to Jewish craftsmen. And certain divisions of the Levites in Judah were assigned to Benjamin, so that no part of the land was left without teachers of the law.

The patriarchs had lived in this land as strangers too. He was looking forward to the city that has foundations, whose designer and builder is God, and God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he has prepared for them a city (Heb 11:10, 16). The tenth who moved to Jerusalem and the nine tenths who stayed in Hebron and Nob and Ono were all waiting for that city. Christ has built it, and in it the lot is not needed. Every one of his people lives there.

11.theology:
A tithe of the people is given to the holy city, some by lot and some by free offering, and those who offer are blessed; it is the mark of the Messiah's people that they offer themselves freely (Ps 110:3). Those who stayed on their inheritance were no less God's people, living on his promise.

Yet all of them, in the city and the villages, still encamped in a shrunken land. They were waiting for the city whose builder is God (Heb 11:10), the holy city coming down from heaven where God dwells with his people and every one of them lives (Rev 21:2-3).
11.examples:
One family in ten moved to Jerusalem: a tithe of the people.

The volunteers were blessed.

Both of Tamar's twins, Perez and Zerah, had descendants in the city.

Some of the priests were mighty men of valor.

A descendant of Asaph led the praise; a Persian king paid the singers.

From Dan to Beersheba had shrunk to Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom.

Nob, where Saul killed the priests, was lived in again.

12.title: Joy Heard Far Away
12.text: <sup>1</sup>These are the priests and the Levites who came up with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,<sup>2</sup>Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,<sup>3</sup>Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,<sup>4</sup>Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,<sup>5</sup>Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,<sup>6</sup>Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,<sup>7</sup>Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah. These were the chiefs of the priests and of their brothers in the days of Jeshua.<sup>8</sup>And the Levites: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, who with his brothers was in charge of the songs of thanksgiving.<sup>9</sup>And Bakbukiah and Unni and their brothers stood opposite them in the service.<sup>10</sup>And Jeshua was the father of Joiakim, Joiakim the father of Eliashib, Eliashib the father of Joiada,<sup>11</sup>Joiada the father of Jonathan, and Jonathan the father of Jaddua.<sup>12</sup>And in the days of Joiakim were priests, heads of fathers' houses: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah;<sup>13</sup>of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan;<sup>14</sup>of Malluchi, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph;<sup>15</sup>of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai;<sup>16</sup>of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam;<sup>17</sup>of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin, of Moadiah, Piltai;<sup>18</sup>of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan;<sup>19</sup>of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi;<sup>20</sup>of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber;<sup>21</sup>of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethanel.<sup>22</sup>In the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, the Levites were recorded as heads of fathers' houses; so too were the priests in the reign of Darius the Persian.<sup>23</sup>As for the sons of Levi, their heads of fathers' houses were written in the Book of the Chronicles until the days of Johanan the son of Eliashib.<sup>24</sup>And the chiefs of the Levites: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua the son of Kadmiel, with their brothers who stood opposite them, to praise and to give thanks, according to the commandment of David the man of God, watch by watch.<sup>25</sup>Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers standing guard at the storehouses of the gates.<sup>26</sup>These were in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and of Ezra, the priest and scribe.<sup>27</sup>And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought the Levites in all their places, to bring them to Jerusalem to celebrate the dedication with gladness, with thanksgivings and with singing, with cymbals, harps, and lyres.<sup>28</sup>And the sons of the singers gathered together from the district surrounding Jerusalem and from the villages of the Netophathites;<sup>29</sup>also from Beth-gilgal and from the region of Geba and Azmaveth, for the singers had built for themselves villages around Jerusalem.<sup>30</sup>And the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people and the gates and the wall.<sup>31</sup>Then I brought the leaders of Judah up onto the wall and appointed two great choirs that gave thanks. One went to the south on the wall to the Dung Gate.<sup>32</sup>And after them went Hoshaiah and half of the leaders of Judah,<sup>33</sup>and Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,<sup>34</sup>Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah,<sup>35</sup>and certain of the priests' sons with trumpets: Zechariah the son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph;<sup>36</sup>and his relatives, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani, with the musical instruments of David the man of God. And Ezra the scribe went before them.<sup>37</sup>At the Fountain Gate they went up straight before them by the stairs of the city of David, at the ascent of the wall, above the house of David, to the Water Gate on the east.<sup>38</sup>The other choir of those who gave thanks went to the north, and I followed them with half of the people, on the wall, above the Tower of the Ovens, to the Broad Wall,<sup>39</sup>and above the Gate of Ephraim, and by the Gate of Yeshanah, and by the Fish Gate and the Tower of Hananel and the Tower of the Hundred, to the Sheep Gate; and they came to a halt at the Gate of the Guard.<sup>40</sup>So both choirs of those who gave thanks stood in the house of God, and I and half of the officials with me;<sup>41</sup>and the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, with trumpets;<sup>42</sup>and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. And the singers sang with Jezrahiah as their leader.<sup>43</sup>And they offered great sacrifices that day and rejoiced, for God had made them rejoice with great joy; the women and children also rejoiced. And the joy of Jerusalem was heard far away.<sup>44</sup>On that day men were appointed over the storerooms, the contributions, the firstfruits, and the tithes, to gather into them the portions required by the Law for the priests and for the Levites according to the fields of the towns, for Judah rejoiced over the priests and the Levites who ministered.<sup>45</sup>And they performed the service of their God and the service of purification, as did the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the command of David and his son Solomon.<sup>46</sup>For long ago in the days of David and Asaph there were directors of the singers, and there were songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.<sup>47</sup>And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah gave the daily portions for the singers and the gatekeepers; and they set apart that which was for the Levites; and the Levites set apart that which was for the sons of Aaron.
12.overview: The chapter opens with the roll of the priests and Levites from the first return to the generation after Nehemiah — six high priests from Jeshua to Jaddua, the heads of the priestly houses (among them of Iddo, Zechariah, almost certainly the prophet), and the Levites who praised antiphonally as David commanded (vv. 1-26). Then the dedication of the wall: Levites and singers gathered from their villages, the people, gates and wall purified (vv. 27-30), and two great choirs of thanksgiving sent along the top of the wall in opposite directions, one led by Ezra, the other followed by Nehemiah, the northern one walking the builders' route of chapter 3 in reverse, until both stand in the house of God (vv. 31-42). God had made them rejoice with great joy; the women and children also rejoiced. And the joy of Jerusalem was heard far away (v. 43). That day men are appointed over the storerooms, for Judah rejoiced over its priests and Levites (vv. 44-47).

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 1–26 — In the Days of Nehemiah the Governor and of Ezra
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The priests and Levites who came up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (vv. 1-9); the high priests from Jeshua to Jaddua (vv. 10-11); the heads of the priestly houses in the next generation, among them of Iddo, Zechariah (vv. 12-21); the Levites recorded down to the days of Darius, who praised according to the commandment of David the man of God, watch by watch (vv. 22-25) — in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and of Ezra, the priest and scribe (v. 26).
verseByVerse.theology: Before the celebration, the roll-call of the men who led the worship for three generations. The joy of verse 43 had a history behind it.

verseByVerse.quote: These are the priests and the Levites who came up with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra, Amariah, Malluch, Hattush, Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth, Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah, Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah, Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah, Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah. These were the chiefs of the priests and of their brothers in the days of Jeshua.
verseByVerse.commentary:
These are the priests and the Levites who came up with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra — twenty-two heads of priestly houses from the first return, ninety years before. (The Ezra here is not the scribe; he came much later.) Among them Abijah (v. 4), the house of John the Baptist's father (Luke 1:5), and Joiarib and Jedaiah (v. 6), whose names head David's list of priestly courses: The first lot fell to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah (1 Chr 24:7).

Why put a list here, just before the dedication? Because the wall was not dedicated by a crowd that had appeared from nowhere. It was dedicated by the heirs of families who had kept the worship going through exile and return. The celebration stands on generations of faithfulness nobody had noticed at the time.

verseByVerse.quote: And the Levites: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, who with his brothers was in charge of the songs of thanksgiving. And Bakbukiah and Unni and their brothers stood opposite them in the service.
verseByVerse.commentary: And the Levites: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, who with his brothers was in charge of the songs of thanksgiving. And Bakbukiah and Unni and their brothers stood opposite them in the service. Two groups of singers facing each other, one answering the other. That is how many psalms were meant to be sung: a line and its reply, for he is good and his steadfast love endures forever. Mattaniah's family kept that thanksgiving going for a century.

verseByVerse.quote: And Jeshua was the father of Joiakim, Joiakim the father of Eliashib, Eliashib the father of Joiada, Joiada the father of Jonathan, and Jonathan the father of Jaddua.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And Jeshua was the father of Joiakim, Joiakim the father of Eliashib, Eliashib the father of Joiada, Joiada the father of Jonathan, and Jonathan the father of Jaddua. Six generations of high priests, from the Jeshua who came home with Zerubbabel to Jaddua, three generations after Eliashib, the high priest of Nehemiah's day. The list has been kept up to date by later hands; verse 22 mentions the reign of Darius the Persian, a king who came after Artaxerxes.

The third name is the Eliashib who built the Sheep Gate (3:1). Hold the fourth. One of the sons of Jehoiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was the son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite (13:28). The line of the high priests ran straight into the family of the enemy. The priesthood of Aaron needed a better Priest than any it could produce: one holy, innocent, unstained, separated from sinners (Heb 7:26).

verseByVerse.quote: And in the days of Joiakim were priests, heads of fathers' houses: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah; of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan; of Malluchi, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph; of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai; of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam; of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin, of Moadiah, Piltai; of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan; of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi; of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber; of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethanel.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And in the days of Joiakim were priests, heads of fathers' houses: for each of the old houses, the man who led it a generation later. Of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah; of Ezra, Meshullam, and so on down the list.

One line in it should stop us. Of Iddo, Zechariah (v. 16). The prophet Zechariah was the son of Berechiah, son of Iddo (Zech 1:1), and Ezra calls him simply Zechariah the son of Iddo (Ezra 5:1). This is almost certainly the same man: the prophet who urged the people to finish the temple was the head of a priestly house. And it was Zechariah who had written, Behold, your king is coming to you; righteous and having salvation is he, humble and mounted on a donkey (Zech 9:9). His name sits quietly in a list of priests, between a Hananiah and a Meshullam. Some of the greatest words ever given to Israel came from a man who appears here as one entry on a roster.

And of Abijah, Zichri (v. 17): the house that would one day have Zechariah the father of John the Baptist in it. The rosters of chapter 12 were running on toward the Gospel of Luke.

verseByVerse.quote: In the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, the Levites were recorded as heads of fathers' houses; so too were the priests in the reign of Darius the Persian. As for the sons of Levi, their heads of fathers' houses were written in the Book of the Chronicles until the days of Johanan the son of Eliashib. And the chiefs of the Levites: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua the son of Kadmiel, with their brothers who stood opposite them, to praise and to give thanks, according to the commandment of David the man of God, watch by watch. Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers standing guard at the storehouses of the gates. These were in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and of Ezra, the priest and scribe.
verseByVerse.commentary:
In the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, the Levites were recorded as heads of fathers' houses ... written in the Book of the Chronicles. The records were kept, generation after generation, in the official books.

And the chiefs of the Levites: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua the son of Kadmiel, with their brothers who stood opposite them, to praise and to give thanks, according to the commandment of David the man of God, watch by watch. The man of God was Moses' title, and here it is David's (as at 2 Chr 8:14), because David ordered the worship of the house as Moses had ordered the tabernacle. The pattern of praise, one choir answering another in shifts, watch by watch, was five hundred years old and still being kept.

The gatekeepers stood guard at the storehouses (v. 25). And the summary: These were in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and of Ezra, the priest and scribe. The governor and the scribe, named together again as at 8:9.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 27–43 — The Joy of Jerusalem Was Heard Far Away
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: For the dedication of the wall the Levites and singers are gathered from their villages, with cymbals, harps and lyres, and the priests purify themselves, the people, the gates and the wall (vv. 27-30). Nehemiah brings the leaders up onto the wall and forms two great choirs: one goes south with Ezra in front (vv. 31-37), the other north with Nehemiah behind it (vv. 38-39), and both come together in the house of God (vv. 40-42). And they offered great sacrifices that day and rejoiced, for God had made them rejoice with great joy; the women and children also rejoiced. And the joy of Jerusalem was heard far away (v. 43).
verseByVerse.theology: Tobiah had said a fox would knock the wall down (4:3). On the day of its dedication two choirs walked along the top of it, singing.

verseByVerse.quote: And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought the Levites in all their places, to bring them to Jerusalem to celebrate the dedication with gladness, with thanksgivings and with singing, with cymbals, harps, and lyres. And the sons of the singers gathered together from the district surrounding Jerusalem and from the villages of the Netophathites; also from Beth-gilgal and from the region of Geba and Azmaveth, for the singers had built for themselves villages around Jerusalem. And the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people and the gates and the wall.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought the Levites in all their places, to bring them to Jerusalem to celebrate the dedication with gladness, with thanksgivings and with singing, with cymbals, harps, and lyres. The wall was finished in Elul (6:15). Its dedication is not dated, but it was not done in a hurry. They sent into every village for the Levites, because the dedication of a wall was to be an act of worship, and worship was their work.

For the singers had built for themselves villages around Jerusalem — Netophah, Beth-gilgal, Geba, Azmaveth. The families of singers lived in a ring of villages round the city, close enough to come in for their turn.

And the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people and the gates and the wall. They purified the stones. The wall was being given to God, and what is given to God is made clean first, beginning with those who give it. The wall that had been built by families with swords at their sides was set apart as holy.

verseByVerse.quote: Then I brought the leaders of Judah up onto the wall and appointed two great choirs that gave thanks. One went to the south on the wall to the Dung Gate. And after them went Hoshaiah and half of the leaders of Judah, and Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam, Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah, and certain of the priests' sons with trumpets: Zechariah the son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph; and his relatives, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani, with the musical instruments of David the man of God. And Ezra the scribe went before them.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Then I brought the leaders of Judah up onto the wall and appointed two great choirs that gave thanks.

Remember Tobiah. Yes, what they are building — if a fox goes up on it he will break down their stone wall! (4:3). Now look at it. The governor brings the leaders of the nation up on top of that wall, and hundreds of people, with trumpets and harps and cymbals, walk along it, singing. The fox's weight was the measure of the enemy's contempt. The wall held a choir.

One went to the south on the wall to the Dung Gate, with half of the leaders of Judah, priests with trumpets, and a descendant of Asaph, Zechariah son of Jonathan, with his relatives playing the musical instruments of David the man of God. And Ezra the scribe went before them. The man who had stood on the wooden platform and read the law from dawn to noon leads the procession on the wall. The Word goes first.

And certain of the priests' sons with trumpets. Moses had given that job to the priests (Num 10:8) and said when to use them: On the day of your gladness also ... you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings ... They shall be a reminder of you before your God (Num 10:10). A reminder, a memorial: the word of Nehemiah's constant prayer, remember. The silver trumpets on the wall were asking God to remember his people on the day of their gladness, and the great sacrifices of verse 43 were what they sounded over.

verseByVerse.quote: At the Fountain Gate they went up straight before them by the stairs of the city of David, at the ascent of the wall, above the house of David, to the Water Gate on the east. The other choir of those who gave thanks went to the north, and I followed them with half of the people, on the wall, above the Tower of the Ovens, to the Broad Wall, and above the Gate of Ephraim, and by the Gate of Yeshanah, and by the Fish Gate and the Tower of Hananel and the Tower of the Hundred, to the Sheep Gate; and they came to a halt at the Gate of the Guard.
verseByVerse.commentary:
At the Fountain Gate they went up straight before them by the stairs of the city of David, at the ascent of the wall, above the house of David, to the Water Gate on the east. Past the old royal quarter, to the gate where the law had been read (8:1).

The other choir of those who gave thanks went to the north, and I followed them with half of the people, on the wall, above the Tower of the Ovens, to the Broad Wall, and above the Gate of Ephraim, and by the Gate of Yeshanah, and by the Fish Gate and the Tower of Hananel and the Tower of the Hundred, to the Sheep Gate.

Read that list against chapter 3 and you will see what it is. Chapter 3 began at the Sheep Gate and ran past the Tower of the Hundred, the Tower of Hananel, the Fish Gate, the Gate of Yeshanah, the Broad Wall and the Tower of the Ovens (3:1-11). The northern choir walks the same stretch in reverse. The stones that Eliashib, the men of Jericho, Meremoth, the goldsmiths and Shallum's daughters had laid are walked over by a choir giving thanks. The builders' work sheet has become a hymn route. And the Tower of Hananel, the landmark of Jeremiah's promise that the city would be rebuilt for the LORD (Jer 31:38), hears the singing.

And Nehemiah does not lead this choir. Ezra goes in front of one; Nehemiah walks behind the other. The governor who had driven the whole work follows the singers.

verseByVerse.quote: So both choirs of those who gave thanks stood in the house of God, and I and half of the officials with me; and the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, with trumpets; and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. And the singers sang with Jezrahiah as their leader.
verseByVerse.commentary:
So both choirs of those who gave thanks stood in the house of God, and I and half of the officials with me; and the priests ... with trumpets; and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar ... And the singers sang with Jezrahiah as their leader.

Two processions set out in opposite directions round the city and meet at the house of God. Every stretch of the wall has been walked and sung over, and everything converges on the place where God had put his name. The wall was never the point. It was built round a people, and the people were gathered round God.

verseByVerse.quote: And they offered great sacrifices that day and rejoiced, for God had made them rejoice with great joy; the women and children also rejoiced. And the joy of Jerusalem was heard far away.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And they offered great sacrifices that day and rejoiced, for God had made them rejoice with great joy; the women and children also rejoiced. And the joy of Jerusalem was heard far away.

Count them: rejoiced, made them rejoice, joy, rejoiced, joy. Five times in one verse. And the source is named: God had made them rejoice. The joy was not the natural relief of a project finished. It was given. Nehemiah had told them that the joy of the LORD was their strength (8:10), and here is that joy, poured out.

The women and children also rejoiced. The wives who had raised the outcry about debt (5:1), the children who had been sold for it (5:5), were singing in the city that had been ruins.

And the joy of Jerusalem was heard far away. Those words were written once before. When the foundation of the temple was laid ninety years earlier, the old men who remembered Solomon's temple wept aloud while the young shouted for joy, so that the people could not distinguish the sound of the joyful shout from the sound of the people's weeping ... and the sound was heard far away (Ezra 3:13). That day the joy and the grief were mixed. This day, only the joy is heard.

It was still not the last word; the next chapter is a sad one. But it was a sound of what was coming. Behold, I bring you good news of great joy that will be for all the people (Luke 2:10). And when the King came down the Mount of Olives toward this city, the whole multitude of his disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice; told to silence them, he said, if these were silent, the very stones would cry out (Luke 19:37, 40). Sanballat had asked whether they could revive the stones (4:2). The King said the stones themselves would sing.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 44–47 — For Judah Rejoiced over the Priests
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: That day men are put in charge of the storerooms for the contributions, firstfruits and tithes, for Judah rejoiced over the priests and the Levites who ministered (v. 44). The priests, singers and gatekeepers serve as David and Solomon commanded (vv. 45-46), and all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah gave the daily portions (v. 47).
verseByVerse.theology: The joy was turned into provision the same day. It is the right order, and the next chapter shows how quickly the provision lapsed when the leader was away.

verseByVerse.quote: On that day men were appointed over the storerooms, the contributions, the firstfruits, and the tithes, to gather into them the portions required by the Law for the priests and for the Levites according to the fields of the towns, for Judah rejoiced over the priests and the Levites who ministered. And they performed the service of their God and the service of purification, as did the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the command of David and his son Solomon. For long ago in the days of David and Asaph there were directors of the singers, and there were songs of praise and thanksgiving to God. And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah gave the daily portions for the singers and the gatekeepers; and they set apart that which was for the Levites; and the Levites set apart that which was for the sons of Aaron.
verseByVerse.commentary:
On that day men were appointed over the storerooms, the contributions, the firstfruits, and the tithes, to gather into them the portions required by the Law for the priests and for the Levites according to the fields of the towns, for Judah rejoiced over the priests and the Levites who ministered.

On the same day as the singing, Nehemiah appoints storekeepers. That is not a fall from joy into bookkeeping. It is joy doing what joy does. For Judah rejoiced over the priests and the Levites: people who are glad of those who serve them want to see them fed. The covenant promises of 10:35-39 were being put into practice.

And they performed the service of their God and the service of purification, as did the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the command of David and his son Solomon. For long ago in the days of David and Asaph there were directors of the singers. The worship was not invented for the occasion. It was the old order, received and kept.

And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah gave the daily portions for the singers and the gatekeepers. It is a summary of the best years, and the next chapter shows how thin it could wear. When Nehemiah came back from Susa, the portions had stopped and the Levites had gone home to their fields (13:10). Joy that is not guarded does not keep. But the sound of verse 43 had been real, and God, who made them rejoice, has promised a city where the joy is never interrupted and the singers never go hungry: they shall hunger no more, neither thirst anymore (Rev 7:16).

12.theology:
The book that began with a man weeping over a burned city (1:4) reaches a city whose joy is heard far away, and the joy is God's gift: God had made them rejoice. The wall was built round a people, and the people were gathered round God; the two choirs end in his house.

The joy is a foretaste. The prophet-priest Zechariah, named in this roll, had promised a King coming to Jerusalem (Zech 9:9); when he came, his disciples rejoiced with a loud voice, and he said the stones would cry out if they were silent (Luke 19:37-40). The last city's joy will not be interrupted (Rev 7:16-17).
12.examples:
The prophet Zechariah appears as one line in a list of priests.

The high priest's grandson married Sanballat's daughter.

They purified the wall itself.

Tobiah said a fox would break it down; two choirs walked on top of it.

The northern choir walked the builders' list of chapter 3 backwards.

Ezra went in front; Nehemiah walked behind.

Five words of joy in one verse, and the women and children singing.

They appointed storekeepers on the day of the celebration.

13.title: Remember Me, O My God
13.text: <sup>1</sup>On that day they read from the Book of Moses in the hearing of the people. And in it was found written that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God,<sup>2</sup>for they did not meet the people of Israel with bread and water, but hired Balaam against them to curse them—yet our God turned the curse into a blessing.<sup>3</sup>As soon as the people heard the law, they separated from Israel all those of foreign descent.<sup>4</sup>Now before this, Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the chambers of the house of our God, and who was related to Tobiah,<sup>5</sup>prepared for Tobiah a large chamber where they had previously put the grain offering, the frankincense, the vessels, and the tithes of grain, wine, and oil, which were given by commandment to the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers, and the contributions for the priests.<sup>6</sup>While this was taking place, I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I went to the king. And after some time I asked leave of the king<sup>7</sup>and came to Jerusalem, and I then discovered the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, preparing for him a chamber in the courts of the house of God.<sup>8</sup>And I was very angry, and I threw all the household furniture of Tobiah out of the chamber.<sup>9</sup>Then I gave orders, and they cleansed the chambers, and I brought back there the vessels of the house of God, with the grain offering and the frankincense.<sup>10</sup>I also found out that the portions of the Levites had not been given to them, so that the Levites and the singers, who did the work, had fled each to his field.<sup>11</sup>So I confronted the officials and said, "Why is the house of God forsaken?" And I gathered them together and set them in their stations.<sup>12</sup>Then all Judah brought the tithe of the grain, wine, and oil into the storehouses.<sup>13</sup>And I appointed as treasurers over the storehouses Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites, and as their assistant Hanan the son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, for they were considered reliable, and their duty was to distribute to their brothers.<sup>14</sup>Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and do not wipe out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God and for his service.<sup>15</sup>In those days I saw in Judah people treading winepresses on the Sabbath, and bringing in heaps of grain and loading them on donkeys, and also wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of loads, which they brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. And I warned them on the day when they sold food.<sup>16</sup>Tyrians also, who lived in the city, brought in fish and all kinds of goods and sold them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah, in Jerusalem itself!<sup>17</sup>Then I confronted the nobles of Judah and said to them, "What is this evil thing that you are doing, profaning the Sabbath day?<sup>18</sup>Did not your fathers act in this way, and did not our God bring all this disaster on us and on this city? Now you are bringing more wrath on Israel by profaning the Sabbath."<sup>19</sup>As soon as it began to grow dark at the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, I commanded that the doors should be shut and gave orders that they should not be opened until after the Sabbath. And I stationed some of my servants at the gates, that no load might be brought in on the Sabbath day.<sup>20</sup>Then the merchants and sellers of all kinds of wares lodged outside Jerusalem once or twice.<sup>21</sup>But I warned them and said to them, "Why do you lodge outside the wall? If you do so again, I will lay hands on you." From that time on they did not come on the Sabbath.<sup>22</sup>Then I commanded the Levites that they should purify themselves and come and guard the gates, to keep the Sabbath day holy. Remember this also in my favor, O my God, and spare me according to the greatness of your steadfast love.<sup>23</sup>In those days also I saw the Jews who had married women of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.<sup>24</sup>And half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod, and they could not speak the language of Judah, but only the language of each people.<sup>25</sup>And I confronted them and cursed them and beat some of them and pulled out their hair. And I made them take an oath in the name of God, saying, "You shall not give your daughters to their sons, or take their daughters for your sons or for yourselves.<sup>26</sup>Did not Solomon king of Israel sin on account of such women? Among the many nations there was no king like him, and he was beloved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel. Nevertheless, foreign women made even him to sin.<sup>27</sup>Shall we then listen to you and do all this great evil and act treacherously against our God by marrying foreign women?"<sup>28</sup>And one of the sons of Jehoiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was the son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite. Therefore I chased him from me.<sup>29</sup>Remember them, O my God, because they have desecrated the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites.<sup>30</sup>Thus I cleansed them from everything foreign, and I established the duties of the priests and Levites, each in his work;<sup>31</sup>and I provided for the wood offering at appointed times, and for the firstfruits. Remember me, O my God, for good.
13.overview: The law is read against Ammonites and Moabites, and the people separate those of foreign descent (vv. 1-3) — while, it turns out, Eliashib the priest has given Tobiah the Ammonite the temple storeroom meant for the Levites' tithes during Nehemiah's absence at the Persian court (vv. 4-6). Returning, Nehemiah throws out Tobiah's furniture and cleanses the rooms (vv. 7-9). The Levites have gone back to their fields for want of their portions; Why is the house of God forsaken? — he restores them and appoints faithful treasurers (vv. 10-14). Grain, wine and Tyrian fish are being traded on the Sabbath; he reminds the nobles why the city burned, shuts the gates before the Sabbath and sets Levites to guard them (vv. 15-22). Jews have married women of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab, and their children cannot speak the language of Judah; he confronts them, cites Solomon, and drives away the high priest's grandson, Sanballat's son-in-law (vv. 23-29). He cleanses and orders the priesthood, provides for the wood offering and firstfruits, and prays: Remember me, O my God, for good (vv. 30-31).

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 1–9 — In the Courts of the House of God
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The Book of Moses is read, and the people find that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God, because Ammon and Moab hired Balaam to curse Israel, yet our God turned the curse into a blessing; and they separate those of foreign descent (vv. 1-3). But before this, while Nehemiah was back at the Persian court, Eliashib the priest had given Tobiah the Ammonite the temple storeroom for the tithes (vv. 4-6). Nehemiah returns, very angry, throws Tobiah's furniture out, has the chambers cleansed, and restores the vessels and offerings (vv. 7-9).
verseByVerse.theology: The law was read against the Ammonite, and the Ammonite was already living in the temple. What the wall had kept out for fifty-two days, the priest's family had let in through a side door.

verseByVerse.quote: On that day they read from the Book of Moses in the hearing of the people. And in it was found written that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God, for they did not meet the people of Israel with bread and water, but hired Balaam against them to curse them—yet our God turned the curse into a blessing. As soon as the people heard the law, they separated from Israel all those of foreign descent.
verseByVerse.commentary:
On that day they read from the Book of Moses in the hearing of the people. And in it was found written that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God, for they did not meet the people of Israel with bread and water, but hired Balaam against them to curse them — yet our God turned the curse into a blessing.

The law is still being read, as it was at the Water Gate, and still being obeyed: as soon as the people heard the law, they separated from Israel all those of foreign descent. The passage is Deuteronomy 23:3-5. Ammon and Moab had refused a thirsty people bread and water in the wilderness and hired a prophet to curse them, and the law shut them out of the assembly.

Two things keep this from being read as a verdict on blood. The first is Ruth. She was a Moabite, and she is David's great-grandmother (Ruth 4:17), because she said your people shall be my people, and your God my God (Ruth 1:16) and came, as Boaz said, under whose wings you have come to take refuge (Ruth 2:12). The law closed the door to Moab the nation; it never closed it to a Moabitess who came to the LORD. The second is the last line: our God turned the curse into a blessing. That is what he does. Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us ... so that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles (Gal 3:13-14). The door shut on Ammon and Moab has been opened by the cross to every Ammonite and Moabite who comes.

verseByVerse.quote: Now before this, Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the chambers of the house of our God, and who was related to Tobiah, prepared for Tobiah a large chamber where they had previously put the grain offering, the frankincense, the vessels, and the tithes of grain, wine, and oil, which were given by commandment to the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers, and the contributions for the priests.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Now before this, Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the chambers of the house of our God, and who was related to Tobiah, prepared for Tobiah a large chamber where they had previously put the grain offering, the frankincense, the vessels, and the tithes of grain, wine, and oil.

Now before this. The chapter has just read the law excluding Ammonites, and the next sentence reveals that an Ammonite was already living in the temple. Tobiah the Ammonite, who had mocked the wall (4:3), plotted against it (4:7-8), hired a prophet to frighten Nehemiah (6:12) and written him threatening letters (6:19), had been given a room in the courts of the house of God — by the man in charge of those rooms, who was related to him by marriage.

And not just any room. It was the storeroom, the chamber for the tithes that the covenant had promised (10:37-39), given by commandment to the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers. The Levites' food had been moved out to make room for the enemy's furniture. The wall had kept Tobiah out for fifty-two days of siege. Family loyalty let him in without a fight.

verseByVerse.quote: While this was taking place, I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I went to the king. And after some time I asked leave of the king and came to Jerusalem, and I then discovered the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, preparing for him a chamber in the courts of the house of God. And I was very angry, and I threw all the household furniture of Tobiah out of the chamber. Then I gave orders, and they cleansed the chambers, and I brought back there the vessels of the house of God, with the grain offering and the frankincense.
verseByVerse.commentary:
While this was taking place, I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I went to the king. Twelve years after he arrived (5:14), Nehemiah went back to the king, as he had promised (2:6). And after some time I asked leave of the king and came to Jerusalem. How long he was away we are not told. Long enough.

And I then discovered the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah ... And I was very angry, and I threw all the household furniture of Tobiah out of the chamber. Picture it: the governor of Judah carrying an Ammonite's couches and chests out of a temple storeroom and dropping them in the courtyard. Then I gave orders, and they cleansed the chambers, and I brought back there the vessels of the house of God, with the grain offering and the frankincense. Out with the enemy, in with the cleansing, back with the things of God.

Some four and a half centuries later another man walked into the temple courts and found them full of trade. Making a whip of cords, he drove them all out of the temple ... do not make my Father's house a house of trade, and his disciples remembered that it was written, Zeal for your house will consume me (John 2:15-17). Nehemiah cleared one room for a season. Christ's zeal for his Father's house consumed him, and it was his own body, he said, that would be the temple raised in three days (John 2:19-21).

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 10–14 — Why Is the House of God Forsaken?
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The Levites' portions have not been given and they have gone home to their fields (v. 10). So I confronted the officials and said, Why is the house of God forsaken? He puts the Levites back at their posts, and all Judah brings the tithes; he appoints reliable treasurers (vv. 11-13). Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and do not wipe out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God and for his service (v. 14).
verseByVerse.theology: We will not neglect the house of our God (10:39) — and the word for neglect is the word for forsaken here. The promise had lasted only while someone was watching.

verseByVerse.quote: I also found out that the portions of the Levites had not been given to them, so that the Levites and the singers, who did the work, had fled each to his field. So I confronted the officials and said, "Why is the house of God forsaken?" And I gathered them together and set them in their stations. Then all Judah brought the tithe of the grain, wine, and oil into the storehouses. And I appointed as treasurers over the storehouses Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites, and as their assistant Hanan the son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, for they were considered reliable, and their duty was to distribute to their brothers.
verseByVerse.commentary:
I also found out that the portions of the Levites had not been given to them, so that the Levites and the singers, who did the work, had fled each to his field. The tithes had stopped, so the men who led the worship had gone back to their farms to feed their families, and the temple had fallen quiet. The singers of chapter 12, whose joy was heard far away, were out in the fields.

So I confronted the officials and said, Why is the house of God forsaken? Forsaken is the verb they had used when they swore, We will not neglect the house of our God (10:39), and it is the verb of the great prayer, in which God did not forsake them (9:17, 19). God had not forsaken his people through nine centuries of rebellion. His people had forsaken his house as soon as their governor was out of sight.

Nehemiah does not only rebuke. I gathered them together and set them in their stations. Then all Judah brought the tithe of the grain, wine, and oil into the storehouses. And he appointed treasurers — a priest, a scribe, a Levite and an assistant — for they were considered reliable. Reliable is the Hebrew for faithful, the word used of Hananiah (7:2) and of Abraham's heart (9:8). Money for God's work was to be handled by faithful men: it is required of stewards that they be found faithful (1 Cor 4:2).

verseByVerse.quote: Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and do not wipe out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God and for his service.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and do not wipe out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God and for his service.

Wipe out is the word Nehemiah used against his enemies in chapter 4: let not their sin be blotted out from your sight (4:5). There he asked God not to blot out their sins; here he asks God not to blot out his good deeds. He is not claiming to have earned heaven. He is asking that the service done for God's house, which the people had so quickly undone, would not be lost from God's record as it had been lost from theirs.

Every believer who has given years to a work and watched it unravel knows this prayer. And the gospel answers it more fully than Nehemiah could have hoped. God does not only keep his servants' good deeds on record; he does something far greater with their bad ones. I, I am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake, and I will not remember your sins (Isa 43:25). The record of debt against us has been cancelled, nailing it to the cross (Col 2:14), and of the one who belongs to Christ he says, I will never blot his name out of the book of life (Rev 3:5).

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 15–22 — To Keep the Sabbath Day Holy
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Men are treading winepresses and bringing loads into Jerusalem on the Sabbath, and Tyrians are selling fish in the city (vv. 15-16). Nehemiah rebukes the nobles: Did not your fathers act in this way, and did not our God bring all this disaster on us and on this city? (vv. 17-18). He shuts the gates from dusk before the Sabbath, sets guards, and warns off the merchants camping outside the wall (vv. 19-21), then sets the Levites to guard the gates: Remember this also in my favor, O my God, and spare me according to the greatness of your steadfast love (v. 22).
verseByVerse.theology: The gates built to keep out Sanballat are shut to keep the Sabbath. And the governor who asks to be remembered asks, in the same breath, to be spared by God's steadfast love.

verseByVerse.quote: In those days I saw in Judah people treading winepresses on the Sabbath, and bringing in heaps of grain and loading them on donkeys, and also wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of loads, which they brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. And I warned them on the day when they sold food. Tyrians also, who lived in the city, brought in fish and all kinds of goods and sold them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah, in Jerusalem itself! Then I confronted the nobles of Judah and said to them, "What is this evil thing that you are doing, profaning the Sabbath day? Did not your fathers act in this way, and did not our God bring all this disaster on us and on this city? Now you are bringing more wrath on Israel by profaning the Sabbath."
verseByVerse.commentary:
In those days I saw in Judah people treading winepresses on the Sabbath, and bringing in heaps of grain and loading them on donkeys, and also wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of loads, which they brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. And Tyrians also, who lived in the city, brought in fish and all kinds of goods and sold them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah, in Jerusalem itself! Nehemiah's exclamation is in the text: in Jerusalem itself! The covenant had said, we will not buy from them on the Sabbath (10:31). The fish stalls were open.

Then I confronted the nobles of Judah and said to them, What is this evil thing that you are doing, profaning the Sabbath day? Did not your fathers act in this way, and did not our God bring all this disaster on us and on this city?

He is quoting history, and behind the history a prophet. Jeremiah had stood at the gates of this city and said, do not bear a burden on the Sabbath day or bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem, and warned that if they did, I will kindle a fire in its gates, and it shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem (Jer 17:21, 27). They did, and the gates burned. Those burned gates were the news that broke Nehemiah's heart in Susa (1:3). Now, with new gates barely hung, donkeys loaded with grain were walking through them on the Sabbath. Now you are bringing more wrath on Israel.

verseByVerse.quote: As soon as it began to grow dark at the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, I commanded that the doors should be shut and gave orders that they should not be opened until after the Sabbath. And I stationed some of my servants at the gates, that no load might be brought in on the Sabbath day. Then the merchants and sellers of all kinds of wares lodged outside Jerusalem once or twice. But I warned them and said to them, "Why do you lodge outside the wall? If you do so again, I will lay hands on you." From that time on they did not come on the Sabbath. Then I commanded the Levites that they should purify themselves and come and guard the gates, to keep the Sabbath day holy. Remember this also in my favor, O my God, and spare me according to the greatness of your steadfast love.
verseByVerse.commentary:
As soon as it began to grow dark at the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, I commanded that the doors should be shut and gave orders that they should not be opened until after the Sabbath. The doors he had hung (7:1) were built to keep out Sanballat. Now they are shut to keep the Sabbath. The wall had become a servant of holiness.

The merchants camped outside the wall once or twice, waiting for the gates to open or for customers to slip out. Why do you lodge outside the wall? If you do so again, I will lay hands on you. From that time on they did not come on the Sabbath. Then he replaced his own servants at the gates with Levites, purified, to keep the Sabbath day holy, so that the guarding of the day was itself an act of worship.

Remember this also in my favor, O my God, and spare me according to the greatness of your steadfast love. Here is the key to all Nehemiah's remember me prayers. In the same sentence in which he asks God to remember his service, he asks God to spare him, and grounds the request in God's hesed, his steadfast love. The man who kept the Sabbath knew he still needed mercy. A Christian can pray both halves of that sentence and should: Lord, remember what I have done for you; and Lord, spare me, not because of it, but because of your love.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 23–31 — Remember Me, O My God, for Good
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Jews have married women of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab, and half their children cannot speak the language of Judah (vv. 23-24). Nehemiah confronts them, curses them, beats some and pulls out their hair, and makes them swear; Did not Solomon king of Israel sin on account of such women? (vv. 25-27). The high priest's grandson is Sanballat's son-in-law, and Nehemiah drives him away: Remember them, O my God, because they have desecrated the priesthood (vv. 28-29). He cleanses the people, orders the priests and Levites, provides for the wood offering and the firstfruits: Remember me, O my God, for good (vv. 30-31).
verseByVerse.theology: The book ends with a prayer, not a triumph. The man who rebuilt the wall could not rebuild a heart, and he knew it. His last words ask God to remember him — and a dying thief, centuries later, asked the same of Jesus and was answered, today you will be with me in paradise (Luke 23:43).

verseByVerse.quote: In those days also I saw the Jews who had married women of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab. And half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod, and they could not speak the language of Judah, but only the language of each people. And I confronted them and cursed them and beat some of them and pulled out their hair. And I made them take an oath in the name of God, saying, "You shall not give your daughters to their sons, or take their daughters for your sons or for yourselves.
verseByVerse.commentary:
In those days also I saw the Jews who had married women of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab. And half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod, and they could not speak the language of Judah, but only the language of each people.

The children could not speak the language of Judah. Think back to the Water Gate, where the law was read and explained so that the people understood the reading (8:8). These children could not have understood a word of it. They could not follow the psalms of Asaph or the prayers of the Levites. The marriages of chapter 13 were producing a generation shut out of the Word of God by the language they had grown up speaking at home. That is the real cost, and it is a warning to every Christian home: children learn the language of what is loved at the table.

And I confronted them and cursed them and beat some of them and pulled out their hair. And I made them take an oath in the name of God. The record is honest about Nehemiah's methods. Ezra, faced with the same sin, pulled out his own hair (Ezra 9:3); Nehemiah pulled out theirs. He acted as the king's governor, with a governor's power to punish. Scripture reports it; it does not hold it up as the pattern for Christ's church, whose servant must not be quarrelsome but kind to everyone ... correcting his opponents with gentleness (2 Tim 2:24-25).

verseByVerse.quote: Did not Solomon king of Israel sin on account of such women? Among the many nations there was no king like him, and he was beloved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel. Nevertheless, foreign women made even him to sin. Shall we then listen to you and do all this great evil and act treacherously against our God by marrying foreign women?"
verseByVerse.commentary:
Did not Solomon king of Israel sin on account of such women? Among the many nations there was no king like him, and he was beloved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel. Nevertheless, foreign women made even him to sin.

He argues from the best example Israel had. Beloved by his God: at his birth God had named him Jedidiah, beloved of the LORD (2 Sam 12:25). Wiser than any man, blessed beyond any king. And the women he married had him build shrines on the hill east of Jerusalem, for Chemosh the abomination of Moab, and for Molech the abomination of the Ammonites (1 Kgs 11:7). Moab and Ammon: the very peoples of verse 23. If the wisest king in Israel's history was drawn away by it, nobody in Jerusalem was safe.

Shall we then listen to you and do all this great evil and act treacherously against our God by marrying foreign women? Act treacherously is the word of Nehemiah's first prayer: If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you (1:8). The sin that had once ended in exile was being committed again inside the rebuilt wall.

verseByVerse.quote: And one of the sons of Jehoiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was the son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite. Therefore I chased him from me. Remember them, O my God, because they have desecrated the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites.
verseByVerse.commentary:
And one of the sons of Jehoiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was the son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite. Therefore I chased him from me.

Sanballat, the man who had jeered at the feeble Jews and plotted to kill their governor, had married his daughter into the high priest's own family. The law required the high priest to marry a virgin of his own people (Lev 21:14), and this was the high priest's own grandson. The enemy who could not get over the wall had married into the priesthood. Nehemiah drove him out.

Remember them, O my God, because they have desecrated the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites. This one is remember them, not remember me. The prophet Malachi, who seems to have preached at about this time, said the same to the priests: You have corrupted the covenant of Levi, and Judah ... has married the daughter of a foreign god (Mal 2:8, 11). The priesthood of Aaron was failing from the top. It needed a Priest whose covenant could not be corrupted, and whose bride would be made clean by his own blood.

verseByVerse.quote: Thus I cleansed them from everything foreign, and I established the duties of the priests and Levites, each in his work; and I provided for the wood offering at appointed times, and for the firstfruits. Remember me, O my God, for good.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Thus I cleansed them from everything foreign, and I established the duties of the priests and Levites, each in his work; and I provided for the wood offering at appointed times, and for the firstfruits.

That is his summary of a life's work, and it ends on the firewood. The wood offering the people had arranged by lot (10:34), so that the fire on the altar would never go out, and the firstfruits. Not the wall, not the fifty-two days, not the king's favour. The fire kept burning and the first of the harvest brought to God. He had learned what matters.

Remember me, O my God, for good. For good is the word of chapter 2, where the good hand of God was on him and the people strengthened their hands for the good work (2:8, 18). And it is the last line of his book. Not a triumph, but a prayer. He had rebuilt a wall, and he could not rebuild a heart. The reforms he had made once he had to make again, and he knew he might have to make them a third time. So he handed the account to God.

Four and a half centuries later, on a hill outside the walls of this same city, a dying thief prayed almost the same prayer: Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom. And he was answered at once: Truly, I say to you, today you will be with me in paradise (Luke 23:42-43). Paradise is the Persian word for the king's park, the forest from which Nehemiah had asked timber for Jerusalem's gates (2:8). The man who built with the king's timber prayed to be remembered. The King who hung on the timber remembers everyone who asks, and brings them into his paradise, where the wall never needs rebuilding and nothing unclean ever gets in. I will be merciful toward their iniquities, and I will remember their sins no more (Heb 8:12). Remembered for good, and their sins forgotten.

13.theology:
Every promise of chapter 10 — marriages, Sabbath, tithes, the house of God — is found broken. The law was good; the covenant was sincere; the heart was unchanged. Nehemiah could rebuild a wall and reform a city, but not write the law on a heart. That needs the new covenant (Jer 31:33), in which God says, I will remember their sins no more (Heb 8:12).

His three prayers in this chapter to be remembered (vv. 14, 22, 31) rest on God's steadfast love, not his record (v. 22). Their answer is the King who, crucified outside this city, answered a thief's remember me with today you will be with me in paradise (Luke 23:42-43).
13.examples:
The law against Ammonites was read while an Ammonite was living in the temple.

The Levites' storeroom had been emptied for Tobiah's furniture.

The singers whose joy was heard far away had gone back to their fields.

Fish for sale in Jerusalem on the Sabbath — in Jerusalem itself!

The gates built against Sanballat were shut against the Sabbath trade.

Children who could not speak the language of Judah could not have understood the reading of the law.

Sanballat's daughter married into the high priest's family.

His last recorded act was providing firewood; his last words, Remember me, O my God, for good.
